anchor: Large language models are served interactively, under explicit latency targets, from GPU fleets whose cost dominates the service's economics.
claim_text: LLM serving is interactive with explicit latency targets and GPU fleet cost dominates economics

anchor: Serving systems decompose inference into stages of distinct computational character, each provisioned separately: prefill and decode run in dedicated worker pools, above engines that batch and schedule tokens, under datacenter-scale orchestration frameworks.
claim_text: Serving systems decompose into prefill/decode pools with separate provisioning, token batching/scheduling engines, and datacenter orchestration

anchor: Multimodal models add one stage: a vision encoder converts the request's images into the embedding tokens the language model consumes, and modality-disaggregated architectures give that encoder a pool of its own.
claim_text: Multimodal models add vision encoder stage; modality-disaggregated architectures give encoder its own pool

anchor: A constant-fraction model (vision work as a fixed multiple of request rate) explains only R^2=0.123 of the image-rate series but R^2=0.654 of decode demand.
claim_text: Constant-fraction model explains 12.3% of image-rate variance vs 65.4% of decode demand variance

anchor: The image signal is also an order of magnitude burstier, and its extremes do not co-occur with the request signal's: the week's largest burst drives image load to nearly sixteen times its weekly mean while the request rate barely moves.
claim_text: Image signal is ~10x burstier than request signal; largest burst drives image load to ~16x weekly mean while request rate barely moves

anchor: The image signal's long-range-dependence exponent is the strongest of the four (Hurst ≈0.93 versus 0.83 for requests).
claim_text: Image signal Hurst exponent ≈0.93 vs 0.83 for requests

anchor: Onsets ramp from baseline to peak in a median of six minutes.
claim_text: Burst onsets ramp from baseline to peak in median 6 minutes

anchor: Against replica cold starts of tens of seconds to minutes, a third of the bursts arrive too fast for a policy that waits to observe them.
claim_text: ~33% of bursts arrive too fast for reactive policy given replica cold starts of tens of seconds to minutes

anchor: The arrival process is overdispersed at every tested operational scale (the Fano factor grows nearly three orders of magnitude with the counting window).
claim_text: Fano factor grows ~1000x with counting window; overdispersed at all tested scales

anchor: In the two-pool simulation, the encoder pool violates its tail-latency target at the trace's own recorded rate: p99 encoder delay reaches 5.0 s at 29% mean utilization.
claim_text: Encoder pool p99 delay reaches 5.0s at 29% mean utilization, violating tail-latency target

anchor: The Qwen3-VL family (8B, 32B, 235B variants) share one vision tower, so the calibrated encoder model and burst-saturation result transfer across the family.
claim_text: Qwen3-VL 8B/32B/235B share vision tower; encoder model and saturation results transfer

anchor: A 235B-TP8 spot-check finds its saturation knee below the 8B's --- decoder scale shrinks only the language pool's envelope, leaving the vision pool untouched.
claim_text: 235B-TP8 saturation knee below 8B; decoder scale shrinks only language pool envelope

anchor: Forecasting uses three pretrained time-series foundation models (TimesFM-2.0, Chronos-2, and Toto-2.0) against naive, exponential-smoothing, and Holt-Winters baselines, under one rolling-origin protocol.
claim_text: Three foundation models (TimesFM-2.0, Chronos-2, Toto-2.0) vs three classical baselines under rolling-origin protocol

anchor: The vision pool is an event-driven FIFO of encoder workers costed by aiconfigurator (AIC), NVIDIA's offline planner, over performance data collected on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090.
claim_text: Vision pool uses AIC-costed encoder workers on RTX 5090 with event-driven FIFO

anchor: The language pool is simulated by Dynamo's discrete-event engine (dynamo.replay with a KV-aware router) under AIC-calibrated H100 timing.
claim_text: Language pool simulated by Dynamo's dynamo.replay with KV-aware router under AIC-calibrated H100 timing

anchor: The model under study is the Qwen3-VL family: the 8B, 32B, and 235B variants share one vision tower.
claim_text: Qwen3-VL 8B/32B/235B share vision tower

anchor: The trace records image counts, not sizes, so the encoder pool assumes a uniform 448^2 image.
claim_text: Encoder pool assumes uniform 448x448 images since trace only has counts not sizes

anchor: Its cost model is validated against the serving engine's own vision tower within 12.8% across the serving regime.
claim_text: Cost model validated against vLLM vision tower within 12.8%

anchor: The inter-pool handoff is priced single-stream: at Qwen3-VL's full DeepStack payload the 588 ms floor and the 0.62x result assume an embedding-only handoff or a ≥100 Gbps fabric.
claim_text: Handoff assumes embedding-only or ≥100 Gbps fabric; 588ms floor and 0.62x result depend on this

anchor: The simulation is open-loop and deterministic, with no speculative encoder-prefill overlap.
claim_text: Simulation is open-loop, deterministic, no speculative encoder-prefill overlap

anchor: Language-pool results characterize the 8B at TP1 but deploy it at TP2×2, with a 235B-TP8 spot-check.
claim_text: Language pool: 8B characterized at TP1, deployed at TP2×2; 235B-TP8 spot-check

anchor: The burst-window language pass at TP2 is token-accounting-convention-dependent while the TP1 prefill floor and the vision-pool verdict are not.
claim_text: TP2 language pass depends on token accounting convention; TP1 prefill floor and vision verdict do not

anchor: Forecasts are zero-shot, the conservative reading of the foundation models' capability.
claim_text: Forecasts are zero-shot (conservative reading)

anchor: Both policies, replayed against the live Dynamo runtime (real control plane, mocked engines) on the fastest-onset burst, reproduce the simulated verdicts in both directions --- TTFT p99 within 1.1-6.8%, provisioned replica-time within 8%.
claim_text: Live Dynamo replay matches simulation: TTFT p99 within 1.1-6.8%, replica-time within 8%

anchor: The physical encoder-worker anchor remains future work.
claim_text: Physical encoder-worker validation is future work

anchor: The empirical basis is AzureLMMInferenceDataset2025, the production trace Microsoft released with ModServe: one million requests over seven days of a multimodal inference cluster.
claim_text: AzureLMMInferenceDataset2025: 1M requests over 7 days from multimodal inference cluster

anchor: Exactly half the requests are text-only; image-bearing requests carry k×k grids, and the frames class of video-like requests (grids larger than 10×10, only 2.7% of all requests) accounts for 81.2% of all image volume.
claim_text: 50% text-only; frames class (>10x10 grids, 2.7% of requests) accounts for 81.2% of image volume

anchor: The trace's four demand signals (requests, images, context tokens, and generated tokens per second) are the trace-derived offered-work signals a scaling policy can watch.
claim_text: Four demand signals: requests, images, context tokens, generated tokens per second

anchor: Chapter 3 establishes that these signals are not interchangeable.
claim_text: Chapter 3 shows signals are not interchangeable

anchor: Nor would watching the right signal reactively suffice.
claim_text: Reactive scaling on correct signal is insufficient

anchor: Aggregation does not rescue the reactive loop: the arrival process is overdispersed at every tested operational scale.
claim_text: Aggregation doesn't fix reactive loop; overdispersion at all tested scales

anchor: The failure is also invisible to the dashboards reactive systems watch.
claim_text: Failure invisible to reactive system dashboards

anchor: The signals that carry the vision pool's load are not only the burstiest but the most persistent.
claim_text: Vision pool signals are both burstiest and most persistent

anchor: The provisioning gap is a lead-time problem, and the lead time is available --- to a forecaster.
claim_text: Provisioning gap is lead-time problem; lead time available to forecaster

anchor: RQ1: Does the request-rate signal carry the information needed to provision each pool? Chapters 3 and 5 answer no for the vision pool and largely yes for decode.
claim_text: RQ1: Request-rate signal insufficient for vision pool (R^2=0.12), largely sufficient for decode

anchor: RQ2: Are the per-pool signals forecastable at provisioning horizons, zero-shot, by pretrained time-series models? Chapter 4 answers yes: foundation models beat every tested classical baseline.
claim_text: RQ2: Per-pool signals forecastable zero-shot; foundation models beat all classical baselines

anchor: Accuracy decays only marginally across the horizon covering the median burst onset, and covariates are nearly irrelevant at provisioning cadence.
claim_text: Forecast accuracy decays marginally over median burst onset horizon; covariates nearly irrelevant

anchor: RQ3: Can the two-pool system be simulated defensibly enough to carry autoscaling conclusions? Chapters 4 and 5 build that platform.
claim_text: RQ3: Two-pool simulation platform built in Chapters 4-5 for autoscaling conclusions

anchor: The collected encoder operator agrees with physical measurement, a matched-engine check validates the composed forward against the serving engine's own vision tower (vLLM).
claim_text: Encoder operator matches physical measurement; matched-engine check validates against vLLM vision tower

anchor: The language pool's calibrated timing exposes the tails the simulator's default polynomial flattens.
claim_text: Calibrated language pool timing exposes tails that polynomial model flattens

anchor: RQ4: Does provisioning each pool on its own signal hold tail-SLA compliance through burst episodes that defeat a reactive planner, and reduce GPU-hours against the best static configuration? Chapters 6 and 7 answer yes.
claim_text: RQ4: Per-pool provisioning holds tail-SLA through bursts, reduces GPU-hours vs best static

anchor: Anticipatory headroom, not signal choice, carries the encoder pool.
claim_text: Anticipatory headroom (not signal choice) carries encoder pool

anchor: A measured tail-aware conversion --- not loop tuning --- repairs the mean-based sizing defect every reactive configuration shares.
claim_text: Tail-aware conversion (not loop tuning) fixes mean-based sizing defect in reactive configs

anchor: Scripted, GPU-accelerated analysis establishes the decoupling, burst anatomy, and persistence contrast.
claim_text: GPU-accelerated analysis establishes decoupling, burst anatomy, persistence contrast

anchor: The full forecast set is archived with the metric tables (Appendix).
claim_text: Full forecast set archived with metric tables

anchor: The RTX 5090 onboarded as a new AIC system; encoder-attention and bf16-GEMM datasets collected at locked clocks in the production container and upstreamed (draft PR ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator#1312).
claim_text: RTX 5090 added to AIC; encoder-attention and bf16-GEMM datasets collected at locked clocks, upstreamed in PR #1312

anchor: The kernel-time ledger closed against a physical measurement of the same network on the same silicon (collected attention operator within ≈3%, the GEMM stratum ≈6%).
claim_text: Kernel-time ledger vs physical measurement: attention within ~3%, GEMM within ~6%

anchor: AIC has no usable encoder-timing fallback, so support-matrix PASS entries on uncollected systems certify text-only costing.
claim_text: AIC has no encoder-timing fallback; PASS entries on uncollected systems = text-only costing

anchor: Unlocked consumer-GPU clocks silently inflate collected data by ≈17% while leaving validation ratios unchanged.
claim_text: Unlocked consumer GPU clocks inflate collected data ~17%; validation ratios unchanged

anchor: A probe-verified exact batching law (encoder cost depends only on total images per forward) with an analytic handoff bound.
claim_text: Encoder cost depends only on total images per forward (exact batching law); analytic handoff bound

anchor: The quantified calibrated-versus-polynomial timing delta.
claim_text: Calibrated vs polynomial timing delta quantified

anchor: Saturation knees an order of magnitude apart on steady traffic.
claim_text: Saturation knees ~10x apart on steady traffic

anchor: The largest burst breaking the two pools in structurally different ways (a shape-fixable prefill floor in the language pool; in the encoder pool, the invisible episodic queueing fixable only by capacity).
claim_text: Largest burst breaks pools differently: language pool has shape-fixable prefill floor; encoder pool has invisible episodic queueing fixable only by capacity

anchor: The static-optimal worker-grid frontier per window, the reactive SLA-planner baseline that satisfies its own window-mean control law while violating the tail SLA.
claim_text: Static-optimal worker-grid frontier; reactive SLA-planner satisfies window-mean but violates tail SLA

anchor: The p90-forecast policy holds the SLA on every forecast-covered window at every forecast-issued lead.
claim_text: p90-forecast policy holds SLA on all forecast-covered windows at all leads

anchor: Prices the covered week at 0.62× the deployable static encoder fleet's worker-time.
claim_text: Forecast policy costs 0.62x static encoder fleet worker-time

anchor: The reactive controller on the same signal loses the fastest-onset burst at every lead.
claim_text: Reactive controller on same signal loses fastest-onset burst at every lead

anchor: The language pool needs a derived tail-aware conversion as the second necessary ingredient.
claim_text: Language pool requires tail-aware conversion as second necessary ingredient

anchor: A calibrated-EWMA control shows the band shape --- supplied zero-shot by the foundation models --- to be load-bearing, not point-forecast accuracy alone.
claim_text: Calibrated-EWMA shows forecast band shape (from foundation models) is load-bearing, not point accuracy

anchor: The evaluation SLA's bounds are a design choice whose sensitivity Chapter 5 quantifies.
claim_text: Evaluation SLA bounds are design choice; sensitivity quantified in Chapter 5

anchor: Intermediate family members unpriced.
claim_text: Intermediate Qwen3-VL family members not priced

anchor: The workload is one seven-day production trace with a by-construction 50/50 modality split and arrival-side information only.
claim_text: Workload: 7-day trace, 50/50 modality split, arrival-side info only

anchor: The stamped decode series is faithful in total volume but temporally displaced, licensing no pointwise provisioning claim in either direction.
claim_text: Decode series faithful in volume but temporally displaced; no pointwise provisioning claims

anchor: The earlier ≈1.4-1.6× figure being execution-stack-specific (Appendix).
claim_text: Earlier 1.4-1.6x validation figure was execution-stack-specific
